notes: §1985:XIV.3.3.3 SR4: "Literal-1 or the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 must be defined as alphanumeric." CommunicationBinder#BindPath binds the KEY operand and refuses COBOL6171 when #IsAlphanumericKey fails; for a data item it asks #IsCommunicationAlphanumericArea of Place.Item, the item as declared, so a reference modification is ignored. §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5 makes a reference-modified numeric, numeric edited or alphanumeric edited item "class and category alphanumeric", so ENABLE ... WITH KEY K-NUM (1:2) is legal and is refused. Probes at 85 (ENABLE OUTPUT): refused numeric, PIC A, ZZ9, S9(3)V9, -1, LENGTH and NUMVAL functions, a witness-like numeric item; accepted X, XBX, a group, "PW", SPACE, ZERO, ALL "A", K-T (I), UPPER-CASE, CHAR (66), CURRENT-DATE (1:4); rejected K-NUM (1:2). The KEY phrase is refused at 2002 on (COBOL0902). Siblings with the same cause: DISABLE KEY K-NUM (1:2) at 85 and RECEIVE INTO K-NUM (1:2) at 2002 (A.2.5.2 SR2) are refused COBOL6171 too. kb/Work PB5384 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read3/rd-06.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Literal-1 or the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 must be defined as alphanumeric."; 2023: "No ENABLE statement; the Communication module is not in 2023 and no candidate covers ENABLE.". ENABLE is a Communication module statement. No 2023 candidate covers it. The candidates are rules of CALL, CANCEL, SEND (message), COPY and other statements.
